about: Table Flip Guy is a rage comic drawing of a stick figure leaping out of a chair, mouth wide open in a scream, as he hurls a table up and away with motion lines flying everywhere. It is the illustrated version of the text emoticon (╯°□°）╯︵ ┻━┻, the universal shorthand for losing your temper so completely that the furniture has to go. People use it for the moment patience runs out: a game crash before a save, a printer jam, a team losing in the last minute.
origin: Flipping a table in anger is a long-running gag in manga, anime and comedy. Online it spread first as a Japanese text emoticon, which Western gamers picked up through online games and chat, and the stick-figure drawing became the rage comic panel for the same feeling.
usage:
The top box describes the build-up and the bottom box delivers the last straw. For example: "the wifi drops" / "during the final boss". The flip is the reaction, so the text only needs to explain what pushed you over the edge.

It lands best for frustrations that are small but infuriating: autocorrect, a loading screen at 99%, a spoiler in the comments, a referee decision. Exaggeration is the point, so the pettier the trigger, the funnier the overreaction looks.
